answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger makes fake identities costly: each agent locks tokens before it can transact, and proven fraud slashes the bond. Like a meadow where every new shoot needs sunlight, each identity needs real resources to grow. The zenith of this design is that Sybil cost scales linearly — an attacker cannot clone a thousand agents without staking a thousand bonds — while honest agents earn their stake back. One dune of sand is cheap to fake; a whole desert is not.
